content.text: I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all six figure briefs against the disclosure and the affirmative USER passages in the conversation.

input.summary: Full source-fidelity preflight run. I built a complete ledger: every limitation of all twenty claims (device 1-10, system 11-15, method 16-20), every one of the seventeen numbered parts in draft/numerals.md (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 34, 36, 38, 40, 42, 44, 46, 48), every sentence of the Field, Background, Summary, Brief Description of the Drawings, Detailed Description and Abstract, and all six figure briefs (FIG. 1 through FIG. 6) were traced to an exact affirmative passage in input/disclosure.md or to the one affirmative USER passage in input/conversation.md ("we can add small stirring elements and let the vibrations cause a constant forward motion"). The remaining USER turns are operational resume/repair instructions and were treated as context only, not as technical support; the drafting agent's own YOU turns were likewise excluded. The core apparatus ledger traces cleanly: rigid base with first and second sides, vibration motor on the first side, air-extraction mechanism (vacuum pump) on the first side in fluid communication with a chamber on the second side, rigid low-friction loop/skirt at the perimeter of the second side, plastic/metal/PTFE/combination materials, no complete airtight seal, restricted-but-continuing inflow beneath the perimeter, continuous extraction maintaining sub-atmospheric chamber pressure, holding force without operator downforce, rigid all-member vibration path with substantially less damping than a flexible suction cup, free sliding to successive areas without releasing the hold, guiding handles, and the rope/wire/cable pulling element with decoupled position-versus-hold control. The autonomous third embodiment, stirring elements 48 and claims 10/15 trace to the single affirmative USER passage above. Terminology is uniform across claims and description (bearing face, clearance, vibration transmission path, volumetric extraction rate, closed loop, exposed face); each numeral denotes one part in every brief; claim antecedent basis is complete; section lines 2-2 and 4-4 carry the same designation in the FIG. 3 source-view brief, the FIG. 2 and FIG. 4 resulting-view briefs, the Brief Description of the Drawings and the Detailed Description; every figure is referenced in the description; and no drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction to a person, or unresolved alternative remains in any application section. Three defects were found and are reported below: (1) a substantive internal inconsistency in the FIG. 2 brief, which directs a "closed housing" on a continuously hatched slab with a plain solid line along every join, so the sheet cited in the description for the air-extraction mechanism withdrawing air from chamber 22 affirmatively depicts an unbroken solid barrier between them, contradicting the "in fluid communication with the chamber" limitation of claims 1, 11 and 16; (2) an untraced extent statement in the Detailed Description asserting that a prior-art air film lies beneath a sliding base "over the whole area of that sliding base", where the disclosure says only that "a thin layer of air between the base and the tile may dampen vibration transfer"; and (3) a verbalized uniform radial width for the functional bearing surface in the FIG. 3 brief ("a single frame of one width"), which is a functional-surface geometry relationship the disclosure never gives, the disclosure reciting only that the perimeter of the second side "is formed as a rigid loop or skirt". Each fix is confined to the figure brief or removes the untraced words, and none recommends adding a speculative shape or optional embodiment to the application text.

findings.title: FIG. 2 brief depicts a sealed solid barrier between the air-extraction mechanism and the chamber, contradicting the "fluid communication" limitation
findings.where: figures/FIG-2-VERTICAL-SECTION-THROUGH-THE-CHAMBER.md, "Geometry to be drawn"; cf. draft/08-detailed-description.md ("The air-extraction mechanism") and draft/09-claims.md claims 1, 11, 16
findings.detail: FIG. 2 is the only view that shows both the air-extraction mechanism 20 and the chamber 22, and the Detailed Description cites it for exactly that relationship. The brief, however, directs "one closed housing standing on the slab", a slab "filled with regularly spaced parallel hatching", and "Where two of them meet, a plain solid line is drawn along the join", with "The housing lies outside the cut, in plain outline with open paper inside." As written, the sheet affirmatively renders an unbroken, closed solid barrier between the interior of the air-extraction mechanism 20 and the chamber 22. That contradicts the specification ("The air-extraction mechanism 20 is coupled to the first side 14 of the base 12, as seen in FIG. 2, and withdraws air from the chamber 22") and the express limitation in claims 1, 11 and 16 that the air-extraction mechanism is "in fluid communication with the chamber". A communication path is affirmatively disclosed by the inventor, so depicting it is source-supported; depicting a closed barrier is not.
findings.evidence: Brief: "and one closed housing standing on the slab, the air-extraction mechanism 20" ... "The housing lies outside the cut, in plain outline with open paper inside." Description: "The air-extraction mechanism 20 is coupled to the first side 14 of the base 12, as seen in FIG. 2, and withdraws air from the chamber 22." Claim 1: "an air-extraction mechanism coupled to the first side and in fluid communication with the chamber". Disclosure: "An air-extraction mechanism, such as a vacuum pump, is also coupled to the first side and is in fluid communication with a chamber located on a second side of the base."
findings.fix: In the FIG. 2 brief, change "one closed housing standing on the slab, the air-extraction mechanism 20" to "one housing standing on the slab, the air-extraction mechanism 20", and after the sentence "The housing lies outside the cut, in plain outline with open paper inside." add: "A plain unhatched gap interrupts the hatching of the slab beneath the housing and runs through the slab from the inside of the housing to the chamber 22, so that the air-extraction mechanism 20 reads as being in fluid communication with the chamber 22; the gap is shown schematically, its width and its position along the slab being a depiction convention for this sheet only, and no port, duct, valve or other passage structure being asserted." No application text changes.

findings.title: Untraced extent asserted for the prior-art air film ("over the whole area of that sliding base")
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, section "The vibration transmission path", second sentence of the final contrast paragraph
findings.detail: The description states that where a prior-art air film remains it lies between the sliding base and the covering element "over the whole area of that sliding base". The disclosure discloses only that a thin layer of air may lie between the base and the tile and may dampen vibration transfer; it says nothing about the film covering the whole area of the base. The whole-area extent is the load-bearing premise of the contrast drawn in the paragraph (partial clearance versus a film across the entire interface), so it conveys technical substance rather than being incidental phrasing, and it appears in the Detailed Description rather than in the Background, where prior-art characterization would need no inventor support.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "Where a film of that kind remains beneath a sliding base of that kind, it lies between that sliding base and the covering element beneath it over the whole area of that sliding base, so that what crosses the interface crosses the film, and the film may dampen the vibration crossing it." Nearest source (no affirmative passage on extent exists): "A smooth sliding base must be pressed firmly against the tile by the operator, and even then a thin layer of air between the base and the tile may dampen vibration transfer."
findings.fix: Delete the untraced extent: replace "it lies between that sliding base and the covering element beneath it over the whole area of that sliding base, so that what crosses the interface crosses the film" with "it lies between that sliding base and the covering element beneath it, so that what crosses the interface crosses the film". Leave the rest of the paragraph, including the hedged modality and the following sentences about the bearing face 26, unchanged.

findings.title: FIG. 3 brief verbalizes a uniform radial width for the functional bearing surface
findings.detail: The ring in FIG. 3 is the perimeter member 24 seen from beneath, i.e. the functional low-friction bearing surface that carries the vibration into the covering element and slides over it. The brief directs that it "reads as a single frame of one width", which verbalizes a constant radial width for that functional face and fixes the radial position of its inner boundary all the way round. The disclosure gives no width, no inner boundary and no uniformity for the loop; it recites only that the perimeter of the second side is formed as a rigid loop or skirt of low-friction material. A plain closed frame outline is an acceptable depiction convention here because the source affirmatively discloses the loop, but the sheet must not verbalize the undisclosed uniform-width relationship, which the existing "rectangular plan form is a convention" disclaimer does not cover.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "The surface between those edges runs unbroken from one to the other along every side, so the view reads as a single frame of one width." Nearest source (no affirmative passage on width or uniformity exists): "The perimeter of the second side is formed as a rigid loop or skirt made from a low-friction material such as plastic, metal, PTFE, or a combination of rigid materials."
findings.fix: In the FIG. 3 brief, replace "The surface between those edges runs unbroken from one to the other along every side, so the view reads as a single frame of one width." with "The surface between those edges runs unbroken from one to the other along every side, so the view reads as one continuous closed frame; the drawn width of that frame is a depiction convention for this sheet only, no particular width, and no uniformity or variation of width, of the perimeter member 24 being asserted." Leave the rest of the brief, the section-line directions and the numeral targets unchanged; no application text changes.
